failures.criterion: 2. Nothing else the listener delivers changes, and nothing arrives twice: the eight stored subjects, an agent's own inbox among them
failures.evidence: An inbox message to a serving-port session arrives twice when a second machine's listener shares the bus and can reach the session's recorded host. Every machine's listener has its own durable and so takes every notifications.agent.* message; the listener that does not own the session goes down session.HandleAgentMessage's registry path, and hostFor now gives it entry.Host for another machine's session (internal/session/session.go:199), where before it dialled the owning listener's machine id, which is no address of a session whose host differs from it. Real surface: listeners m1 (ENVOY_HOST_BRIDGE=127.0.0.1) and m2 on one nats-server; the session registered through m1 by envoy-client's own subscribe (host = kernel hostname, port 18901); POST /v1/messages/send to it -> base binary d6cf8f38: 1 prompt (m2 logs 'listener agent session not found anywhere'); head d73383ee: 2 prompts, both m1 and m2 log 'listener agent delivered' for event 808695a415ecf041de2072fdaf50cc5e. This is the deployment's shape: the cluster the production record uses runs two listeners of different machine ids on one bus (the in-cluster listener and the one beside Dispatch), and agent pods there are reached at their pod address. Red test (own commit 44bace59): TestAnInboxMessageReachesAServingPortOnceWithAnotherMachinesListenerOnTheBus in packages/envoy/cmd/listener/live_topics_test.go; `cd packages/envoy && go test ./cmd/listener/ -run TestAnInboxMessageReachesAServingPortOnceWithAnotherMachinesListenerOnTheBus -count=1` fails at the head: 'received another prompt within 3s, want none'. Counter-check in a scratch copy only: with hostFor using entry.Host for the listener's own machine alone, this test, TestAServingPortReceivesATopicTheStreamDoesNotStore and TestAListenerReachesASessionAtTheHostItRecorded all pass. Which fix is right is the architect's call: the approved spec's address rule names the recorded host for another machine's session too, while its criterion 2 forbids the second arrival.
